bib.title: Do Better ImageNet Models Transfer Better?

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Table I.1 numeric cells skimmed, not recorded individually.

question: Do ImageNet architectures that score higher on ImageNet also transfer better to other image classification tasks, as fixed features, fine-tuned, or trained from scratch?
hypothesis: Implicit community assumption that better ImageNet models transfer better, and learn better features; the paper tests it rather than asserting it.
contributions: Better ImageNet networks provide better penultimate layer features for transfer learning with linear classification (r = 0.99), and better performance when the entire network is fine-tuned (r = 0.96).
Regularizers that improve ImageNet performance are highly detrimental to the performance of transfer learning based on penultimate layer features.

Architectures transfer well across tasks even when weights do not: on two small fine-grained datasets fine-tuning gives little benefit over random init, but better ImageNet architectures still score higher.

method.summary: Retrain 16 CNNs on ImageNet with matched settings (BN scale, no label smoothing/dropout/aux head), then evaluate on 12 classification datasets in three settings: L2 logistic regression on frozen penultimate features, full fine-tuning, and training from random init. Correlate ImageNet top-1 with transfer accuracy on logit scale.

datasets.name: ImageNet (ILSVRC 2012)
datasets.split: ~50,000 train images held out as validation to choose training length, then full train
datasets.preprocessing: preprocessing and augmentation from TF inception_preprocessing [79]

datasets.name: 12 transfer datasets (Food-101, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Birdsnap, SUN397, Stanford Cars, FGVC Aircraft, PASCAL VOC 2007 Cls, DTD, Oxford-IIIT Pets, Caltech-101, Oxford 102 Flowers)
datasets.size: 2,040 to 75,750 training images (20 to 5,000 per class); Table 1 gives per-dataset train/test
datasets.split: provided splits; validation set from train where none given; DTD and SUN397 first split only; Caltech-101 30 train/class, rest test; final results retrained on train+val
datasets.preprocessing: images rescaled to each network's ImageNet input size

models.name: 16 CNNs: Inception v1, BN-Inception, Inception v3, v4, Inception-ResNet v2, ResNet-50/101/152 v1, DenseNet-121/169/201, MobileNet v1, v2, v2 (1.4), NASNet-A Mobile, NASNet-A Large (VGG appears in some figures)
models.params: 2.2M (MobileNet v2) to 84.7M (NASNet-A Large), excluding logits layer
models.init_from: retrained on ImageNet by the authors (public checkpoints used only for Appendix B, Sec 4.6-4.7)

training.objective: ImageNet classification (cross-entropy implied); transfer by logistic regression, fine-tuning, or from scratch
training.lr: ImageNet: linear warmup to 1.6 then x0.975 per epoch; fine-tune: grid of 7 log-spaced values 0.0001 to 0.1; from scratch: 0.001 to 1.0
training.lr_schedule: ImageNet: exponential decay 0.975/epoch; fine-tune: cosine decay
training.batch_size: ImageNet 4096; fine-tune and from scratch 256 (64 / 16 for dataset-size study)
training.steps: fine-tune and from-scratch 20,000 steps; logistic regression with augmentation 40,000 steps
training.epochs: ImageNet: up to 300 in held-out run, then the best-performing step count
training.weight_decay: ImageNet 8e-5; fine-tune/scratch: grid of 7 weight-decay-to-lr ratios 1e-6 to 1e-3 (scratch 1e-5 to 1e-2), plus none
training.dropout: none in the main setting (varied in ablation)
training.regularisation: main setting: BN scale on, no label smoothing, dropout, aux head; NASNet-A Large drop path disabled; EMA of weights decay 0.9999
training.seeds: single run per model in main results; 3 fine-tuning runs x 2 tuning rounds in Fig C.3; 3 subsets in Fig 9

other.logreg: multinomial L2 logistic regression, L-BFGS, 45 log-spaced L2 values 1e-6 to 1e5 on validation, no augmentation, full image
other.svm: scikit-learn, C from 26 log-spaced values 0.001 to 100, L2-normalised features
other.dataset_size_study: fine-tune >=1000 steps or 100 epochs, batch 64, lr range /4; scratch >=78,125 steps or 200 epochs, batch 16, lr range /16, public Inception v4 checkpoint

other.eval_crop: uncropped vs central 87.5% crop chosen on validation (fine-tuning)

metrics.name: transfer accuracy
metrics.definition: top-1 for most datasets; mean per-class for Aircraft, Pets, Caltech-101, Flowers; 11-point mAP for VOC2007; analysed as logit(accuracy) (log odds) averaged over datasets

metrics.name: Pearson r (and Spearman rho)
metrics.definition: correlation between logit ImageNet top-1 and dataset-averaged logit transfer accuracy across 16 models

baselines: Published state of the art per dataset (Table F.1)
SVM and augmented logistic regression (Appendix G)
eval.protocol: Permutation test / exact McNemar test per dataset pair; t-test across datasets; Morey-corrected error bars; Wilcoxon signed rank for fine-tune vs logreg. Tests compare trained models, not architectures (no variance over random inits).

evidence.quote: trained all networks with a batch size of 4096 using Nesterov momentum of 0.9 and weight decay of 8 × 10−5

results.setup: 16 CNNs, 12 datasets, logistic regression on penultimate features, logit scale

results.quote: we found that ImageNet top-1 accuracy was highly correlated with transfer accuracy (r = 0.96)

limits: Tests compare trained models, not architectures: no variance over random initialisations or data order is measured (A.1.1).
Fine-tuning hyperparameters were chosen on large validation sets, so results may not reflect small-data practice (A.5).
Only CNNs on image classification; 16 architectures, one training run each, so r values rest on 16 points.
Retrained NASNet-A Large reached 80.8% vs 82.7% published because regularisers were disabled.
Authors concede few-shot/adaptable-feature methods were not tested; open question how to adapt ImageNet features better.
Public-checkpoint analysis shows conclusions depend on training recipe, so architecture ranking is recipe-dependent.

terms.definition: logit(p) = log(p/(1-p)); additive change delta is a multiplicative change exp(delta) in the odds of correct classification

figures.caption: Transfer learning performance is highly correlated with ImageNet top-1 accuracy for fixed ImageNet features (left) and fine-tuning from ImageNet initialization (right).
ImageNet training settings have a large effect upon performance of logistic regression classifiers trained on penultimate layer features.
figures.why: shows regularisers help ImageNet but hurt features

figures.caption: Networks pretrained on ImageNet converge faster, even when final accuracy is the same as training from random initialization.
Pretraining on ImageNet improves performance on fine-grained tasks with small amounts of data, but the gap narrows quickly as dataset size increases.
